text:
Welcome to the

2024 Children & Family Game Design Contest

CONTEST RESULTS

Contest Geeklist
Feedback Monitor

This contest is meant to design games that we can play with our children, or games that children can play together. The focus should be on games that children (9 and under) can play with their families. Themes should be appealing, mechanisms should be easy to grasp. As has always been the case, these games should include some player agency. Meaning games where you flip a card or roll a die and move to the next space of the same color are out, unless accompanied with something that requires at least a tiny bit more thought. The following is adapted from the 2020 Children's Game Print & Play Game Design Contest.


Quote:
While the rules should be simple, games should require player choices and action to play. Games should not be decided entirely on random factors instead of player input (such as Candy Land).

Contest Rules

Important Dates
Game submission deadline: April 15th, 2024 (Small edits/tweaks allowed until May 1st, 2024.)
Voting begins: May 1st, 2024
Voting closes: May 15th, 2024

Game Submissions

 Games entered in this contest must have a WIP (Work In Progress) thread entered in the Board Game WIP Forum. The first post of this WIP thread must contain the following:

• A link to the 2024 Children & Family Game Game Design Contest (this thread).
• A brief Game Summary (2 or 3 sentences).
• An image of the game (more than one is fine, but at least one is required). The image may be set up to replicate the game in play.
• Description of components required to play.
• Number of players.
• Intended earliest age to play.
• Approximate playing time.
• Categories in which the game will be competing.
• Links to the current game files. Rules and components should be in PDF format. The files can be hosted on your own webserver, online storage sites (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.) or in your personal BGG image gallery. The files must be freely available to anyone with the link and users should be able to download them without needing to create an account.

All of the above information will be required in the WIP thread. Any other info is at the designer's discretion. Please keep the first post in your WIP thread updated with current links and information about the game.

 Include the current status of your game in the WIP thread's title. This will help other people know where you feel your game is in the design process.

 Idea Phase (Private Playtesting. No publicly available printed components yet.)
 Components Available (Public Playtesting. Printed Components are available. Game may be changed as a result of playtesting.)
 Contest Ready (Game is complete. No changes will be made.)

 Games submitted to this contest should be new or contain significant updates to a previously released game, be it PnP, published, or part of a previous contest. Previously released games may not be entered unchanged.

 To enter a game in the contest, you must also add your WIP thread to the contest GeekList. Only games on the GeekList are officially in the contest!

Submission Limits

Designers or design teams may submit up to 2 games to this contest.

Game Design & Components

 The only design restriction for this contest is that game be appropriate for the intended player age range. Game mechanics, theme, and other considerations open to the designer's discretion. Designers may work in teams, as designers, artists, playtesters, etc.

 There are no limits on quantity of components or rulebook size. Designers should be aware that larger and more complex games may be played by fewer people, and receive correspondingly less feedback. In addition, complex games can be more challenging for children to play and enjoy.

 All games must be printable on regular A4/American Letter Paper. Large format components such as game boards are okay as long as they can assembled from pieces printed on A4/Letter sheets. Here is a useful document for determining the margin size of sheets designed to be printed on either A4 or Letter paper.

 Designers may design any components necessary for their game, but the preferred format for files is PDF.

 Designers may ask players to provide a reasonable number of common game components, including but not limited to pawns, dice, cubes, standard playing cards, etc.

Feedback requirement

Entrants are required to post meaningful feedback on at least two other games for each one that they enter. This requirement will be validated.
If you give feedback out of the game's thread (i.e. by geekmail, on comments on google drive, etc), please send me a note, so it's counted.

Prizes and Categories of Competition

These categories will receive (at least) 200 for 1st place, 150 for 2nd place, and 100 for 3rd place. Please tip this thread if you wish to give to designers participating in this contest.

Two Main Categories

 Children's Game - This is a game intended for young children to play together even without an adult present.
 Family Game - This is a game for adults and children to play together.

Voting
Vote here

The contest includes a two-week period after the submission deadline to play the games and vote. No changes to the rules or components will be allowed during this time.

Copyright

The rights to all games submitted to this contest remain with their designers. You may release your game under any license you wish provided that the files are available for free, legal printing and assembly for personal use during the contest duration.

Designers must have full legal right over the games entered into this contest. Games should not contain artwork or characters that are protected by copyright or trademark without permission from the owner. Games may include content protected by Creative Commons or Copyleft licenses so long as the rules regarding redistribution and derivative works are followed. Artwork or characters in the public domain are allowed.

Digital Versions

Digital adaptations via Tabletop Simulator, Vassal, etc. are allowed in this contest, provided printable PnP components are also available.

FAQ for New Users

If you are new to BGG, Chris Hansen prepared a guide to help introduce you to everything you need to know to enter a game into this contest.
Design Contest FAQ for New Users 

Happy Designing!

The most important part of this contest is to have fun and help each other create and develop fun, new games for the kids! Engaging with each other to build a community encourages better design and creates a better experience for us all. Thank you all in advance for being kind, courteous, and helpful members of this PnP community.

Happy designing!

The contest rules are adapted from those created by Chris Hansen  for the previous Children's Game Print and Play Design Contests, released under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License.
